issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named Meal (with constructor and getters) but the template repository contains an implemented Order class while Meal.java in the template is empty. Additionally, the template Main (commented code) references Order, whereas the problem description, UML and solution use Meal. This naming/type mismatch between Order and Meal is structural and will confuse students about which class to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the type names in the template to match the problem statement and tests: either remove or rename Order.java and provide a proper Meal.java implementation in the template (with the same constructor and getters shown in the UML), and update Main to reference Meal. This ensures students implement and use Meal as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution refer to a Meal class as the domain entity representing a meal, but the template repository provides an Order class that has the exact same structure (name and ingredients). Additionally the template contains an empty Meal.java. This mismatch (Meal vs Order) creates confusion for students mapping the problem description to the starter code and expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem and solution by renaming or replacing the template's Order class to Meal (move the implementation into src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java and remove the redundant Order class), or update the problem statement to reference Order consistently. Ensure the Meal.java in the template is populated with the same fields and getters as in the solution.
